page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a burstable, shared-core virtual machine designed for low-intensity workloads. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is allocated 2 vCPUs, which share 1/8 of a physical core, and supports hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory, providing 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the e2-micro in the bottom 10% across all tested categories. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 132.9, and the multi-core score is 171.0. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with cached small-block reads reaching 9.73 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads drop to 0.1 GB/sec and large-block writes register at 1.33 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 201.56 and 176.45, respectively. In application-level tests, the instance achieves 0.2 million operations per second for Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 0.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-micro represents a highly economical entry-tier option, trading raw processing power and memory capacity for minimal resource consumption. The shared-core CPU allocation introduces potential performance variability depending on host node utilization. Due to these resource limitations, this instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic microservices, development testing environments, low-traffic static web serving, or simple cron jobs.
